newsitem.title: FRANCE: German president to visit synagogue on Paris visit.
newsitem.headline: German president to visit synagogue on Paris visit.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog will meet Jewish leaders and visit the Great Synagogue in Paris at his own request during a state visit to France next week, diplomats said on Friday.

Herzog, whose office is largely ceremonial, will visit France from next Wednesday to Saturday. His synagogue visit on Friday will gesture symbolise German remorse for the persecution of Jews in France during the World War Two occupation.

French President Jacques Chirac last year acknowledged for the first time the responsibility of the French state in aiding and abetting the deportation of some 76,000 Jews to Nazi death camps between 1942 and 1944.
Herzog has not asked to meet either Christian or Moslem leaders on the first state visit by a German president to France since 1984.

He will hold talks with Chirac, Prime Minister Alain Juppe and opposition leaders, visit the southwestern city of Bordeaux and attend conferences on the 18th century French philosopher Montesquieu and on the French Revolution and German unification.

He will also be present for the inauguration of a major exhibition on Berlin, united Germany's capital and soon-to-be seat of government, at the futuristic Grande Arche of La Defense, in Paris, next Thursday.

The German president, a conservative former supreme court president, has invited as personal guests several civil rights campaigners from former East Germany, including artist Baerbel Bohley and Protestant pastor Friedrich Schorlemmer.

Diplomats said his programme was aimed at stressing both the influence of French Enlightenment ideas on the development of civil rights and the separation of powers in postwar Germany, and the integration of the former communist east into the federal republic since fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.
